title: What tenant representation means for a Newcastle business
excerpt: A practical explanation of who a tenant representative works for, where the role fits and what to confirm before you engage one.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: Tenant Representation Newcastle | Your Office Space
metaDescription: Understand what a commercial tenant representative does, who they work for and what Newcastle businesses should confirm before an engagement.
body:
## Start with who the adviser represents

A landlord's leasing agent acts for the property owner. A tenant representative acts for the business looking for, reviewing or negotiating space. That distinction matters because the parties do not carry the same priorities, risks or information.

Tenant representation is commercial property advice from the occupier's side. It does not replace legal, accounting, building or other specialist advice. A good process makes those responsibilities clear before decisions are made.

## Where a tenant representative can help

The agreed scope may include:

- turning operational needs into a clear property brief
- finding and comparing suitable options
- arranging inspections and recording trade-offs
- comparing rent, outgoings, incentives and other commercial terms
- identifying obligations that need legal or technical review
- negotiating agreed commercial points
- coordinating handover into fit out, furniture and move-in planning

The exact scope should be written down. Do not assume every adviser provides every part of the process.

## What to confirm before engaging anyone

Ask who the adviser represents, what is included, how they are paid, which licensing and geographic limits apply, what evidence supports market claims and which decisions still require your approval. The answers should be clear enough to include in the engagement scope.

## When to start

Start before timing removes useful choices. The right lead time depends on the lease, option dates, business requirements, search area and complexity of the workplace. Check the controlling dates, then work backwards from the decision and delivery steps.

If you are considering a new lease, renewal or relocation, begin with the decision you need to make. Your Office Space will confirm whether the brief fits our current capability, licensing and service area before proposing an engagement.

This article is general commercial information, not legal or financial advice.
